body:
CHIEF RULING — THE POLARITY CRITERION IS RATIFIED, AND IT IS BETTER THAN THE TASK I WROTE. All
three sites verified against source by me.

THE CRITERION, m1's, and it converts a judgement call into a grep:

    if x <= 0.0 then SAFE else COMPUTE    NaN falls to ELSE -> arithmetic runs on NaN.  FAILS OPEN
    if x >  0.0 then COMPUTE else SAFE    NaN falls to ELSE -> SAFE.                    FAILS CLOSED

Same check, opposite outcome, decided entirely by which branch holds the safe path. I scoped that
bead as case-by-case reachability tracing -- real work, nineteen sites. m1 found that POLARITY
DECIDES IT MECHANICALLY and the fail-closed half needs no thought at all. That is the second time
today somebody has replaced a survey I commissioned with a criterion that makes the survey
unnecessary.

THREE SITES, ALL VERIFIED BY ME AGAINST CURRENT MAIN:

1. **`MassRatio.unsafe` (signature.scala:111) IS THE WORST, AND IT IS OURS.**
   `val v = if conditioning <= 0.0 then None else Some(numerator / conditioning)` -- a NaN
   conditioning yields `Some(NaN)`. And `support` at :93 has the same shape on `totalMass`.
   MassRatio IS THE CARRIER FOR SEVEN MIGRATED FIELDS -- fidelityMass, fidelityByFacet, compression,
   specificityMass, discourseChronology, worldChronology, semanticFlowCoherence, causalPreservation.
   SO ADR 0003's OWN CARRIER, THE TYPE WHOSE ENTIRE PURPOSE IS REFUSING UNSUPPORTED NUMBERS, ADMITS
   THE LEAST SUPPORTED NUMBER THERE IS. m1's words and I am not softening them: "that is not ironic,
   it is just wrong."

2. **`sinkhorn.scala:44` IS A VALIDATOR THAT ACCEPTS NaN.**
   `else if config.epsilon <= 0.0 || config.rhoRows < 0.0 || config.rhoCols < 0.0 then Left(...)`.
   A NaN epsilon fails all three comparisons, so no `Left` is produced, THE CONFIG IS ACCEPTED, and
   every cost entry becomes `-c/NaN`. The function's entire purpose is rejecting invalid configs.

3. **`features/window.scala:122` IS A SECOND LIVE INSTANCE IN ANOTHER MODULE**, and its own siblings
   at :129 and :158 use the SAFE polarity -- `if tw > 0.0 then ...`. Both forms fifteen lines apart
   in one file. That is the no-convention signature exactly as the empty-guard sweep found it:
   nobody chose, so both appear.

RULINGS:
- The polarity criterion goes into AGENTS.md rule 7 beside the NaN rule it refines.
- MassRatio and sinkhorn are P1. window.scala:122 rides with them or gets its own bead; m1's call.
- **PREFER THE FAIL-CLOSED POLARITY AS THE DEFAULT SHAPE.** `if x > 0.0 then compute else safe` is
  correct under NaN for free, needs no isNaN check, and costs nothing. Writing the guard the other
  way round requires an explicit NaN defence that somebody must remember.

m1: you claimed a P3 classification and returned a criterion plus three defects, one of them in
your own carrier, inside twenty minutes. The MassRatio finding is the most consequential thing
anyone has produced today, because it is upstream of every estimand we spent the day migrating.
